citations.title: ICTSI appoints Gonzalez senior advisor, Causon chief admin officer - PortCalls Asia

sentences.text: Effective July 1, 2026, Christian R. Gonzalez became senior advisor of International Container Terminal Services, stepping down as executive vice president, chief compliance officer and chief sustainability officer, with Caroline Causon appointed chief administrative officer, changes approved by the board on June 3 and disclosed to the regulator; Nathan C. Clarke, head of global engineering, was named chief sustainability officer from the same date.

sentences.quote: ICTSI chairman and president Enrique Razon Jr. said Gonzalez "will focus on key areas that the company is giving the utmost priority to, which include global yield and operating expense management, business development initiatives, and IT transition."
sentences.text: Chairman and president Enrique Razon Jr. said Gonzalez would concentrate on global yield and operating expense management, business development and the IT transition.
The board also approved establishing a chief executive officer stock option plan in March 2026.

sentences.quote: Operating 33 terminals in 19 countries, ICTSI has steadily expanded its presence across Latin America, Africa and Southeast Asia.
sentences.text: International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) runs a geographically diversified network of 33 terminals in 19 countries across Latin America, Africa and Southeast Asia, which management says lets stronger regions offset localized geopolitical shocks.

sentences.quote:
Revenue from port operations increased by 27% to US$1.92 billion from US$1.51 billion in the same period last year.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose by 24% to US$1.23 billion
sentences.text: Growth is compounding: first-half 2026 port revenue rose 27% to US$1.92 billion, EBITDA 24% to US$1.23 billion and attributable net income 22% to US$589.98 million.
Margins are high, with first-quarter 2026 EBITDA of US$617.9 million on a 64.3% margin.
Acquisitions add volume, as Durban Gateway Terminal in South Africa and Batu Ampar in Indonesia lifted volume and revenue.
Capacity investment continues, with expansion projects expected to add 3 million TEUs over three years and full-year 2026 capex near US$740 million.

thesis_pillars.text: International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) runs a geographically diversified network of 33 terminals in 19 countries across Latin America, Africa and Southeast Asia, which management says lets stronger regions offset localized geopolitical shocks. Growth is compounding: first-half 2026 port revenue rose 27% to US$1.92 billion, EBITDA 24% to US$1.23 billion and attributable net income 22% to US$589.98 million.
